intro: Small, sharp tools that do one thing and can prove they did it. Most are a single static binary or run entirely in the browser — no backend, no account, no telemetry. Much of the code is written with coding agents at the keyboard; what ships is what the tests, the CI and the benchmarks let through, and I answer for it. Grouped by what they are; newest first inside each group.

categories.title: LLM & agent tooling
categories.tagline: Instrumenting, measuring and fact-checking what models actually do
categories.intro: The common thread: a claim is not a result. Every one of these exists because something was asserted — a release note, a cost estimate, a changelog — and nothing was checking it.

projects.name: wallii
projects.blurb: append-only message wall for agents: NDJSON feed plus a CLI to post, tail and browse it.
projects.detail: An append-only message wall for agents: NDJSON feed plus a CLI to post, tail and browse it. Agents report finished work — including the failures — so a long-running fleet leaves a readable trail rather than a scrollback.

projects.name: claudii
projects.blurb: statusline for Claude Code: session cost, context %, rate limits, model health. Pure bash + jq, zero daemons.
projects.detail: A statusline for Claude Code: session cost, context usage in percent, rate-limit headroom and model health, refreshed in the prompt. Pure bash and jq — no daemon, no background process, nothing that outlives the shell.

projects.name: bumpii
projects.blurb: reads what changed in the tools you run and keeps only what touches the features you use.
projects.detail: Reads what changed in the CLI tools and containers you run, keeps only what touches the features you use, and then bumps them. The judgement is the point: most upgrade notes matter to somebody, but not to you.

projects.name: check0r3000
projects.blurb: LLM extraction of comparable facts out of insurance terms, benchmarked against golden files. Finding so far: what you feed the model matters more than which model.
projects.detail: Extracts comparable facts out of German insurance terms (AVB), ranks them by quality and tracks prices over time — an entire market in one terminal. Ships with its own benchmark: golden files per line of business, scored on faithfulness, schema validity, hallucinations and coverage, because an extraction pipeline whose accuracy you have not measured is a rumour. Finding so far: what you feed the model matters more than which model — on one contract a local 20B model scored 100 where Opus scored 57, same input.

projects.name: comparereleaseii
projects.blurb: fact-check release notes against the diff that shipped — GitHub, Forgejo, GitLab or any git clone.
projects.detail: Fact-checks release notes against the diff that shipped. Works on GitHub, Forgejo, GitLab or any local git clone. Answers the question you have before an upgrade: does the changelog describe what changed, and what did it leave out?

projects.name: gateii
projects.blurb: minimal self-hosted proxy in front of LLM APIs — OpenResty, Prometheus, Grafana.
projects.detail: A minimal self-hosted proxy in front of LLM APIs. One place that sees every request, so latency, spend and failure rates are measurable instead of anecdotal.

projects.name: cc-insomnii
projects.blurb: a bedtime-shaming statusline for Claude Code.
projects.detail: A bedtime-shaming statusline for Claude Code. Small, and it works.

categories.title: Backup, recovery & proof
categories.tagline: Systems that assume the failure already happened and stay useful anyway
categories.intro: What matters after the bad thing is not that a backup exists, but that it cannot have been rewritten — and that you can show it.

projects.name: stattii
projects.blurb: attestation over an event calendar — cancellations propagate outward with delivery proof.
projects.detail: An attestation layer over an event calendar. Responsible people confirm or cancel through tokenised links; a cancellation propagates outward to everyone downstream, with delivery proof at each hop. Built for the case where "I never got the message" has consequences.

projects.name: how-small-can-we-go
projects.blurb: trust-golf: one champion per task, dethroned by needing less trust. Measured, never claimed.
projects.detail: A trust-golf arena: one champion per task, dethroned by needing less trust — fewer third-party bytes, fewer dangerous constructs. Every entry is measured against the same surface metric, never self-declared, and the current champion is whoever survived the last challenge.

projects.name: revertii
projects.blurb: update a service with the way back built in: snapshot, dead man's switch, health-check, revert.
projects.detail: Updates a service with the way back built in: snapshot, arm a dead man's switch, apply, health-check, and revert automatically if it does not come back. The switch is armed before the change, not after — an update that hangs is the case a manual rollback never covers.

projects.name: baaackaaab
projects.blurb: one-way, ransomware-resistant iCloud backup: Drive and Photos into an append-only restic store.
projects.detail: One-way, ransomware-resistant iCloud backup: Drive and Photos into an append-only restic store. One-way is the whole design — the machine holding the source can write new snapshots but cannot delete old ones, so an attacker with full control of it still cannot reach into yesterday.

categories.title: Local-first web apps
categories.tagline: Static pages that keep your data in your own browser
categories.intro: No backend, no account, no telemetry — which also means there is no server of mine to breach, subpoena or shut down.

projects.name: musiclinkii
projects.blurb: turn one music link into links for every streaming platform.
projects.detail: Turn one music link into links for every streaming platform, so a recommendation stops depending on what the other person subscribes to. Fully static.

projects.name: gymii
projects.blurb: floor-plan your gym, log sets against numbered machines. Offline-first, data never leaves the device.
projects.detail: Floor-plan your gym, then log sets against numbered machines instead of guessing which bench you used. Offline-first, all data in the browser.

projects.name: shieldchipiii
projects.blurb: stone-chip logbook for your windshield, so the insurance conversation has a record instead of a memory.
projects.detail: A stone-chip logbook for your car windshield: photograph and date every chip, so the insurance conversation later has a record instead of a memory. Local-only web app plus a terminal CLI, DE/EN.

projects.name: putzii
projects.blurb: cleaning schedule shared by capability link, with QR check-in. No backend at all.
projects.detail: A cleaning schedule for a shared flat or office, handed around as a capability link and checked in by QR code on the wall. No accounts, no backend — the link is the permission.

projects.name: kuvertii
projects.blurb: read what an email header says about you — who it was really addressed to, where the unsubscribe link leads.
projects.detail: Paste an email header and read what it says about you: who the message was really addressed to, how that address was hidden from the other recipients, and where the unsubscribe link actually leads. Runs entirely client-side — a tool about privacy that uploaded your mail headers would be a joke.

projects.name: db-wallet
projects.blurb: drink tracking wallet for the crowd at bitcircus101.de and Datenburg e.V. Bonn.
projects.detail: Drink tracking wallet for the crowd at bitcircus101.de and Datenburg e.V. Bonn.

projects.name: app-icons-generator
projects.blurb: every iOS, macOS and watchOS icon size from one 1024px PNG — CLI and browser.
projects.detail: Generates every iOS, macOS and watchOS app icon size from one 1024px PNG. Available as a CLI and as a client-side browser tool — the browser version never uploads the image.

categories.title: Terminal & macOS
categories.tagline: Things that live in a shell, or in the menu bar next to it
categories.intro: Mostly single static binaries or a few hundred lines of shell — installable, removable, and readable in one sitting.

projects.name: pegel-visual
projects.blurb: live ASCII water levels for German rivers, with an optional aircraft overlay from your own ADS-B receiver.
projects.detail: Live ASCII water levels for German rivers, straight from PEGELONLINE, with an optional aircraft overlay fed by your own ADS-B receiver. A dashboard that fits in an 80×24 terminal and still tells you whether the river is rising.

projects.name: epcii
projects.blurb: EPC QR code (GiroCode) generator — one static binary with its own QR encoder core.
projects.detail: EPC QR code (GiroCode) generator — a single static binary with its own QR encoder core rather than a dependency tree, so a payment code can be generated on a machine you do not want to install anything on.

projects.name: youtubehistii
projects.blurb: local YouTube watch-history analyzer — topics, and consume vs. learn. Fully on-device.
projects.detail: Analyses your YouTube watch history locally — topics, and the split between consuming and learning. Fully on-device, because handing a full viewing history to a third party to be told how you spend your evenings is a poor trade.

projects.name: vpnii
projects.blurb: VPN status in the zsh prompt, on top of WireGuard and Tailscale.
projects.detail: VPN status indicator for zsh plus a small CLI on top of WireGuard and Tailscale. Answers "am I actually on the tunnel right now" in the prompt, where the question comes up.

projects.name: pwdtintii
projects.blurb: the terminal background takes its colour from the directory you are in. zsh, bash, fish, tmux-aware.
projects.detail: The terminal background takes its colour from the directory you are standing in, via OSC 11 and tmux-aware. The point is not decoration: production and staging stop looking identical at 2am.

projects.name: KeebLock
projects.blurb: locks the keyboard while you clean it, with animations worth the thirty seconds.
projects.detail: Locks the keyboard while you wipe it down, with animations worth watching for the thirty seconds it takes.

projects.name: audioctl
projects.blurb: switch macOS output and input devices, volume, mute and sample rate from the CLI.
projects.detail: Control macOS audio from the CLI: switch the default output and input device, volume, mute and sample rate, and cycle outputs with a global hotkey — the things the system UI makes you click through.

projects.name: git-times-live
projects.blurb: a standalone live broadcast TV channel for your git activity.
projects.detail: A standalone live broadcast TV channel for your git activity, generated from git-times. Exactly as useful as it sounds, and it runs.

categories.title: FreshRSS extensions
categories.tagline: Four small extensions for the reader I actually use every day
categories.intro: Each one exists because a single step in my own reading loop was one click too many.

projects.name: ClickHistory
projects.blurb: keeps a history of the article links you actually opened.
projects.detail: Keeps a history of the article links you actually opened, as opposed to the ones you scrolled past. Turns "I read something about this last month" into a searchable list.

projects.name: ShareViaQRCode
projects.blurb: a large QR code for the current article, so a phone can pick the link off the screen.
projects.detail: Shows a large QR code for the current article, so a phone can pick the link straight off the screen — no sharing service in between.

projects.name: NoteDrop
projects.blurb: drop notes and links on one device, copy them on another with one click.
projects.detail: Drop notes and links from one device and copy them on another with one click — the gap between reading on the phone and acting on the laptop, closed without a chat message to yourself.

projects.name: ExitReaderView
projects.blurb: a floating button to leave the reading view in one click.
projects.detail: Adds a floating button to leave the reading view in one click. Nine commits, and it fixes the thing that annoyed me daily.
